# rusqsieve factorization test corpus
#
# Factorization test corpus for the rusqsieve crate. Each active line is one
# test case:
#
#     N f1 f2 ... fk
#
# space-separated decimal integers: N followed by its complete prime
# factorization in ascending order, so that f1 * f2 * ... * fk == N. Repeated
# factors are listed once per multiplicity. **The arity varies from line to
# line** -- k ranges from 1 (N itself prime) to 10. A parser must read the
# whole line and must not assume exactly two factors.
#
# Lines beginning with '#' are comments. Entries are sorted ascending by the
# bit length of N within each section.
#
# VERIFICATION
#   Every line in this file was verified programmatically before inclusion:
#     * f1 * f2 * ... * fk == N, exact integer equality (Python
#       arbitrary-precision ints)
#     * every factor certified prime by a Baillie-PSW primality test --
#       trial division by primes < 256, then a Miller-Rabin base-2 test,
#       then a strong Lucas probable-prime test (Selfridge Method A).
#       The implementation was cross-checked against a sieve of
#       Eratosthenes for all n < 200000 (zero disagreements) and against
#       known Carmichael numbers and Mersenne primes.
#   Nothing unverified appears in this file.
#
# CONTENTS
#   Entries:            309
#                       (200 carried over from the source corpus,
#                        109 generated for this file)
#   Bit-length range:   7-256 bits
#   Arity:              196 semiprimes (k = 2), 20 with N prime (k = 1),
#                       93 with three or more prime factors (k >= 3)
#   Dense coverage:     >= 3 balanced semiprimes at every bit length from
#                       63 to 90 inclusive
#   Large balanced:     >= 3 each at 128, 160 and 192 bits; >= 2 each at
#                       224 and 256 bits (the crate's advertised range)
#   Also included:      6 deliberately unbalanced (small p, large q) cases
#                       and 36 prime-power (n = p^k, k >= 2) cases, of which
#                       11 are squares, in labelled sections at the end
#
# EXPECTED FAILURES -- REGRESSION CASES, DO NOT PRUNE
#   117 entries have N in the 65-85 bit band, which is the `choose_a` dead
#   zone. 87 of those are semiprimes and fail deterministically on
#   rusqsieve v0.2.0; they are the verified regression set. The other
#   30 entries in the band (8 with N prime, 5 prime powers,
#   17 composites with three or more prime factors) can short-circuit ahead
#   of the sieve via the primality and perfect-power arms of the dispatch
#   ladder, so their v0.2.0 behaviour is not asserted here. All of them are
#   included deliberately as regression cases: once the dead zone is fixed
#   every entry in this file must factor correctly, and none may be removed
#   to make a test pass.
#
# --- MAIN CORPUS: ASCENDING BY BIT LENGTH OF N ---
# Mixed balance and mixed arity. Holds the entries carried over from the
# source corpus (whose factor counts and p:q balance vary widely) together
# with the generated balanced semiprime set. Deliberately unbalanced
# semiprimes and prime-power cases are in their own sections further down.
